events.summary: Arrangements were made to build a temporary Bailey bridge after Batticaloa New Bridge collapsed.
Jaffna Municipal Council began installing newly purchased streetlights across wards.
The Prime Minister officially opened the national scout Poson zone in Colombo.
Officials launched a fast-track identification programme for eligible older people missing their monthly allowance.
Kalubowila Hospital’s new cardiac catheterisation unit is scheduled to open on June 30.
Police security and special traffic measures are being arranged for the Poson festival in Anuradhapura.
Housing assistance was provided to beneficiaries; 21 homes have received initial funding so far.
The local council and residents carried out dengue cleanup at Annooriya School and nearby areas.
Rehabilitation of the flood-prone road is underway under a Northern Province allocation.
Archaeology Department announced a programme to protect 1,000 sites nationwide.
Government employees are to receive 20 kilograms of subsidised rice by instalment payments.
ADB approved a concessional loan for rooftop solar aggregation and virtual net metering.
EU grant supports rooftop solar aggregation and virtual net metering.
Japan Fund grant supports the project's joint lending mechanism.
Deputy energy minister requested a temporary shutdown of rooftop solar systems above 300 units.
Health ministry plans to appoint 2,847 nurses in October 2026.
Government reports 57 billion rupees allocated for ongoing fuel subsidies.
Diesel subsidy rate is 100 rupees per litre.
Government decided to procure 600 buses, with a request to allocate some to Batticaloa.
Government introduced a programme to establish 500 tea villages nationwide.
Railways planned special trains to Anuradhapura for Poson observances.
AIA sponsorship will provide free Anuradhapura–Mihintale trains for three days.
OMP and Bureau of Rehabilitation signed an institutional cooperation memorandum.
Housing assistance cheques of Rs. 350,000 each were issued to 34 beneficiaries.
Officials were directed to complete the India-funded 4,700-home estate project by year-end.
Officials were directed to complete the India-funded 4,700-home estate project by year-end.
Aswesuma payments for two beneficiary categories have stopped, with eligibility limited to poor families.
World Bank-backed RE-VIVE plans $100 million in development investment across the Northern and Eastern Provinces.
Authorities completed preparations for Poson festival services in Anuradhapura.
Sri Lanka formally received ten US-donated TH-57 helicopters; officials signed a bilateral agreement.
The President appointed a commission to address public-sector salary and pension issues.
Colombo launched a three-day drone-assisted dengue inspection and control operation.
United States formally transferred ten TH-57 Sea Ranger helicopters to the Sri Lanka Air Force.
President established the Salary and Pension Commission by gazette to recommend policy and public-service reforms.
United States provided Fleet Broadband satellite communications equipment for Sri Lankan Navy patrol vessels.
Government and railway staff completed repairs to the storm-damaged track.
The first train from Nanu Oya to Badulla resumed service after repairs.
Officials discussed increasing Jaffna–Colombo rail services and revising schedules.
Allocated first-phase funds for college classroom, hostel and assembly hall repairs.
Provided 32 fishing nets to cyclone-affected fishers in three northern districts.
President's Fund spent Rs. 5.8 million providing laptops to 14 university students.
ADB declined the contract award after the selected contractor was blacklisted, halting the road works.
Officials said the road works would be taken up with domestic funding and retendered.
Cabinet approved modernising 126 school hostels during 2026–2028.
Checks issued to 125 Jaffna housing beneficiaries at LKR 400,000 each.
Cabinet increased the allocation per ministry-built house from LKR 1.5 million to LKR 2 million.
827 ministry houses and 281 National Housing Development Authority houses are under construction in Jaffna District.
Kuchchaveli local council supplied drinking water to residents after their complaint.
India delivered military supplies worth USD 5.5 million to the Sri Lanka Army.
Sri Lanka launched its 2026–2030 National Export Development Plan in Colombo.
Police introduced a nationwide online portal for public feedback, complaints, praise and suggestions.
Reconstruction began on the cyclone-damaged Pandiyan Road bridge near Puthukkudiyiruppu.
Government began a six-day nationwide cleanup campaign to curb dengue spread.
Cabinet authorised legal steps to obtain an additional ADB loan for the trade and industry programme.
Cabinet authorised legal steps for ADB’s post-Ditwah reconstruction and livelihood loan.
Labour Ministry began reforms to recognise domestic work and strengthen workers’ rights.
Cabinet approved a national policy to regulate bottled drinking-water prices.
Water officials plan a drought-risk awareness programme beginning June 17.
Minister ordered urgent coordinated dengue-control measures during National Dengue Eradication Week.
Korea-funded biomedical engineering centre modernisation was officially opened.
Medical testing and repair equipment is planned for provincial biomedical service units.
Peradeniya Hospital emergency and accident unit and main laboratory modernisation completed and opened.
Cyclone Ditwah landslide restoration work intensified on the upcountry railway line.
Vadatharakai ferry returned to passenger service after repairs.
Health Minister said recruitment approval for health-sector vacancies is under final discussion.
National dengue eradication week began nationwide with support from ministries and police.
Fuel subsidy payments are to end in June after the allocated funds were exhausted.
Fuel subsidy payments are to end in June after the allocated funds were exhausted.
A newly constructed Koppai Police Station opened at a new site.
Colombo District decided to conduct a special dengue eradication week from June 15 to 21.
The Sasakawa Sri Lanka-Japan Cultural Centre opened in Colombo.
Sri Lanka's Defence Ministry signed an MoU with the Sasakawa Peace Foundation.
President instructed agencies to prepare plans for water, electricity, farming, and food security amid El Niño risks.
Jaffna Municipal Council resolved to seek transfer of the Cultural Centre into its care.
US experts shared budget oversight practices with Sri Lankan parliamentarians.
Parliament extended the committee deadline for its Cyclone Ditwah preparedness report.
Funding was allocated for new production factories for Northern Province cooperatives.
Additional funding was allocated to develop palm toddy production in the Northern Province.
The UN humanitarian plan reached 575,000 people and closed after raising donor contributions.
Government allocated funding for 26 urban public health facility projects under Clean Sri Lanka.
Cabinet approved 5 million rupees and 10 perches of land for each fully damaged estate home.
A boat launching facility was built at Beruwala harbour with a reported 76 million rupee investment.
Construction of the Beruwala boat launching facility was reported as complete.
Stakeholders agreed to transfer facility management and maintenance to the fisheries harbours corporation.
Cabinet approved Rs. 5 million and 10 perches for each fully damaged plantation line room.
Scout association decided to hold a Colombo Poson zone with presidential secretariat coordination.
Three-day dengue-control operation began across 14 high-risk districts.
Vehicle number-plate printing resumed at Werahera after a prolonged suspension.
Government allocated about Rs. 76 billion to resume and complete 25 suspended health construction projects.
A bill to establish the Institute for Chartered Media Professionals was gazetted.
India-funded hybrid renewable energy project across three islands was underway; the High Commissioner reviewed progress.
A tripartite agreement was signed with ADB for a 150 MW wind power project.
Battery storage installation is underway in Vavuniya under the national grid storage project.
Lanka Metro Transit added eight stops to Makumbura–Colombo and Makumbura–Kadawatha routes.
Five forests were declared protected reserves under the Vanaspathi programme.
Elephant corridors were opened in Hambantota and Monaragala districts.
Health Ministry decided on a nationwide three-day dengue control programme for June 8–10.
Task force began cleaning drainage channels near Bandaranaike International Airport roads.
Revenue Management Committee invited public proposals to strengthen medium- and long-term government revenue strategies.
Pakistan announced fully and partially funded scholarships for Sri Lankan students.
The Treasury received the IMF programme’s sixth and seventh loan installments after reviews were completed.
JICA agreed to send a technical team to develop fisheries-sector projects.
An overseas Sri Lankan donor contributed Rs. 10 million to the recovery fund.
The Treasury received the IMF's sixth and seventh EFF loan instalments.
The government allocated Rs. 500 billion for assistance after Cyclone Ditwah.
The government allocated Rs. 100 billion for assistance during the Middle East crisis.
Cabinet approved a further Rs. 20 billion allocation for assistance.
India-funded renewable energy works continued across three Jaffna islands.
Permanent repairs to cyclone-damaged water infrastructure had begun.
Cyclone damage to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board was estimated at Rs. 5 billion.
The annual budget allocated funding for the nationwide health and wellness centres programme.
UNDP-funded initiative is conducting activities to increase women’s participation in politics.
Central Bank launched June financial consumer protection awareness campaign against fraud.
Treasury allocated funds for fuel price relief in April.
Private bus owners requested a 25-rupee-per-litre diesel subsidy.
Allocated funds for cooperative paddy drying and storage improvements.
Paddy-drying machinery programme for cooperative societies is being implemented.
Production and packaging machinery programme for producer cooperatives is underway.
Ten donated TH-57 helicopters arrived and entered modification and technical preparation.
Puttalam-bound train services were temporarily restricted to Madampe after a derailment.
Island campaign recorded 734 sterilizations and 985 rabies vaccinations.
Petroleum Corporation plans stricter enforcement of the national fuel quota system.
Renovation of the National Hospital Neurology Institute cost Rs. 99 million.
Health Minister handed the renovated Neurology Institute over for public use.
Rs. 500 billion was allocated for repairs to Cyclone Ditwah public damage.
Rs. 168 billion of the Cyclone Ditwah repair allocation had been spent.
Work began to restore a main irrigation canal damaged by Cyclone Ditwah.
The 51st Samurdhi Arusuvai restaurant opened in Matale District.
Officials plan to open 100 Samurdhi Arusuvai restaurants by year-end 2026.
Transport deputy minister introduced live tracking for Metro buses through the LMT GO app.
Rehabilitation work began on Aadiyapatham Road near Thirunelveli Junction.
Health Ministry launched a programme to provide five mammography machines to government hospitals.
Japan signed an aid agreement to help Ditwah-affected freshwater fishers rebuild livelihoods.
